title: Migrations are safe across a rolling upgrade
description: Serves "Nothing breaks the viewers' evening.". (mixed-version playback is JS-208). Every dogfood deploy already runs two versions side by side, but upgrade safety is one line at the end of the plan (JS-058). Migrations run with no lock timeout and no check for migrations a newer version applied (internal/db/db.go), an old worker can compute another spec hash than a new one (ARCHITECTURE.md known departures), and docs/running.md and ARCHITECTURE.md disagree on which role rolls first.
acceptanceCriteria: Migrations take a lock timeout and a version that finds a migration newer than it knows refuses to start with a clear message
One documented rollout order, the same in docs/running.md and ARCHITECTURE.md, and a test or check that each migration in a release is safe for the previous version's code

Observed first with real processes under a playing film: a migration that takes exclusive locks on two tables a running worker and a stream replica use is applied while they run. The upgrading replica starts (it applies the migration again after a deadlock or lock timeout) or refuses once with a message naming the lock; it never fails to start silently. No viewer request is answered an error. The record says what a stream replica answers from memory if Postgres stops just after its snapshot read was aborted; a gap there returns to the product owner as a brief and is not built here.
notes: Before JS-054, which adds encoder families to the spec. The version-gated claim moved to JS-082 (2026-11-12). Extended from the Fable 5.2 blind audit, 2026-11-14. When it starts it is split into migrations (criteria 1, 3, 6) and mixed-version play (2, 4, 5).
